notes: The cross-cutting delivery-capacity signal. Read it as a delivered cut whose service effects persist, not as a gap still growing: the reduced response to low-category pollution incidents (SI4), and the recreation, outdoor and climate programme reductions (SI7, SI8), took effect from April 2025 and have not been reversed by the better 2026-27 settlement. Two things pull the other way on capacity: the improved Grant in Aid, and against it the phased budget reductions recouping the 14.6 million pound HMRC settlement (see the IR35 signal). Reframed on 25 July 2026 after verification found the forward-looking 17 million pound framing had gone stale, which is exactly the failure mode the date check exists to catch. The 265-job figure in some coverage was the October 2024 proposal; 233 is the confirmed outcome agreed by NRW's Board on 5 November 2024. A separate 15 million pound gap reported in July 2020 was a COVID-era story and is unrelated.
summary: Natural Resources Wales delivered a 12 million pound savings programme against a funding gap of about 9 million pounds in 2024-25. Senedd Research (8 November 2024) records the removal of 233 posts, closure of visitor-centre cafes and shops and the Bangor library, and, most relevant to the indicators, a reduced response to low-category pollution incidents and cut resources for climate change, recreation and outdoor programmes. The often-quoted 17 million pounds was a projection of the gap by 2026-27 if nothing were done, not an outturn: action was taken, and NRW's Business Plan 2026-27 shows revenue Grant in Aid rising by 8.8 million pounds to 151.5 million, with a further 7.3 million in specific grants for nature recovery, climate action, coal tip safety, waste reform and water quality.
title: NRW's savings programme cut 233 posts and reduced pollution-incident response; the 2026-27 settlement improves
